decisions.reason: As a core airfield lighting control product with clear launch commitment and likely long airport procurement cycles, its option value remains high and the firm would usually keep it on the market.

The surveillance display fits the firm's airport systems portfolio and, absent clear negative evidence, a German industrial supplier would tend to keep such a specialized system available while market potential continues to resolve.
A training program is relatively inexpensive to maintain and supports the installed base, so real-options logic favors keeping it open unless demand has clearly disappointed.
This training course showed the weakest visible commitment and is easy to withdraw or fold into broader service offerings, so management would be more likely to redeploy resources elsewhere.

The collaboration software tool is adjacent to airport operations and still has unresolved upside, making it worth keeping unless ongoing software support costs have become clearly disproportionate to demand.
A multilateration surveillance system is a strategic, high-commitment product in a niche market with long sales cycles, so the firm would normally keep the option alive rather than exit quickly.
